title: Warm Up Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
shortDescription: Warm-up catalyst on Bank 1 not heating fast enough to reduce cold-start emissions.
fullDescription:
P0421 indicates the close-coupled warm-up catalyst on Bank 1 is below efficiency threshold during the cold-start light-off monitor. The PCM uses upstream and downstream O2 sensor activity to score the catalyst's ability to oxidize HC during the first 60 seconds.

A failing warm-up cat raises cold-start hydrocarbons sharply and is a common cause of IM-240 cold-start failures even when the rear cat looks fine.
safetyImpact: Increased emissions; long-term catalyst damage if root cause is engine misfire.

causes.cause: Exhaust leak ahead of upstream O2

fixSteps.title: Check fuel trims at idle
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm STFT/LTFT within ±10% before condemning catalyst.

fixSteps.title: Inspect exhaust for leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Check manifold gasket and pipe joints upstream of O2 sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace warm-up catalyst
fixSteps.instruction: If fueling is correct and exhaust sealed, replace the catalyst.

faq.q: Will a tune fix this?
faq.a: No, the catalyst is monitored by the PCM regardless of tune.

faq.q: Is the warm-up cat the same as the main cat?
faq.a: No, it's a smaller close-coupled unit between the manifold and main cat.

title: Warm Up Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
shortDescription: Warm-up catalyst on Bank 2 not heating fast enough during cold start.
fullDescription:
P0431 mirrors P0421 but for Bank 2 on V-engines. The dedicated warm-up catalyst near the Bank 2 manifold is failing the cold-start light-off test.

On many V6/V8 vehicles both warm-up cats live in the exhaust manifolds and are integrated, so replacement requires the manifold assembly.
safetyImpact: Increased cold-start emissions.

fixSteps.title: Verify Bank 2 fuel trims
fixSteps.instruction: Long-term trims should be within ±10%.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Bank 2 manifold
fixSteps.instruction: Check for cracks and gasket leaks.

fixSteps.title: Replace Bank 2 warm-up cat
fixSteps.instruction: Often integrated with the manifold.

faq.q: Same fix as P0421?
faq.a: Yes but on the opposite cylinder bank.

title: Reductant System Performance
shortDescription: DEF system overall performance below threshold; SCR not reducing NOx adequately.
fullDescription:
P204F is a high-level SCR/reductant performance code that sets when the downstream NOx sensor reports insufficient NOx conversion despite the dosing system commanding DEF injection. It rolls up many possible underlying issues: dosing quantity, mixing, catalyst condition, or sensor accuracy.

The ECM enters a derate countdown (often 200 mi / 55 mph / no-restart depending on tier), so this code must be diagnosed promptly.
safetyImpact: Vehicle will derate and may refuse restart; emissions out of compliance.

causes.cause: Exhaust leak between turbo and SCR

fixSteps.title: Read live NOx sensor data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare upstream vs downstream NOx ppm; conversion should exceed 80% at temp.

fixSteps.title: Test DEF quality
fixSteps.instruction: Use refractometer; urea should be 32.5% ±0.5%.

fixSteps.title: Inspect dosing spray pattern
fixSteps.instruction: Activate dosing test; expect even cone with no dribble.

fixSteps.title: Replace SCR catalyst if conversion low
fixSteps.instruction: After ruling out sensors and dosing.

faq.q: Why is my truck about to derate?
faq.a: Heavy-duty emissions regs require a stepped derate when SCR fails to keep NOx in spec.

faq.q: Can I just clear the code?
faq.a: It will return as soon as the dosing monitor runs again at temperature.

title: Reductant Quality Performance — Quality Below Threshold
shortDescription: DEF concentration is out of the 32.5% urea spec window.
fullDescription:
This variant of the reductant quality fault is set specifically when the quality sensor (or NOx-conversion-derived quality model) determines the urea concentration is too far from 32.5%. Common causes are watered-down DEF, expired DEF that has decomposed, or accidental refill with washer fluid or diesel.

Unlike P207F base code, this variant focuses on concentration rather than presence.
safetyImpact: Derate sequence active; emissions noncompliant.

causes.cause: Wrong fluid added to DEF tank

fixSteps.title: Test DEF with refractometer
fixSteps.instruction: Should read 32.5% urea.

fixSteps.title: Drain and refill with fresh DEF
fixSteps.instruction: From a sealed certified container.

fixSteps.title: Reset adaptation after refill
fixSteps.instruction: Run forced regen / quality re-learn.

faq.q: How do I know if my DEF is bad?
faq.a: Refractometer reading outside 32.0-33.0% urea or yellow tint indicates contamination.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1) — Soot Loading Model
shortDescription: DPF soot loading model and pressure feedback indicate the filter no longer captures particulates.
fullDescription:
This P2002 variant focuses on the soot-loading model output: the ECM's calculated PM efficiency derived from differential pressure, exhaust flow, and ash mass. When the model concludes the substrate is cracked, melted or no longer trapping, this code is set.

A real efficiency failure differs from a regen-fault chain (P2463/P2459); here the filter physically can't trap soot regardless of pressure.
safetyImpact: Excessive PM emissions; possible derate.

causes.cause: Cracked or melted DPF substrate (post-runaway regen)
Failed differential pressure sensor reading low

fixSteps.title: Read DPF soot/ash grams
fixSteps.instruction: Soot stuck near 0 with high flow indicates substrate failure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect DPF outlet for soot leakage
fixSteps.instruction: Black soot at the tailpipe after long highway run is diagnostic.

fixSteps.title: Replace DPF assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Replace if substrate is compromised; not a cleanable condition.

faq.q: Can a clogged DPF cause this?
faq.a: No — clogged sets pressure-side codes; this code means the filter has lost its trapping ability.

title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent Bank 1 Sensor 1
shortDescription: EGT sensor 1 Bank 1 reading is dropping in/out intermittently.
fullDescription:
P2081 sets when the ECM detects an electrical or rationality fault on the indicated exhaust gas temperature sensor. EGT sensors are critical inputs for DPF regen control, turbo overtemp protection, and SCR catalyst dosing strategy.

A wrong EGT reading either prevents regen from initiating or, worse, can trigger an over-temperature regen that damages the DPF substrate.
safetyImpact: Regen may not run; possible thermal damage if temperature is misread upward.

fixSteps.title: Read sensor live data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare to other EGT sensors at idle; should agree within 30 °C.

fixSteps.title: Resistance check
fixSteps.instruction: EGT thermistors typically 200 Ω–10 kΩ depending on type and temp.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM-spec sensor; threadlock per spec.

faq.q: Can I clean an EGT sensor?
faq.a: Wiping soot off the tip can help but a failed thermistor must be replaced.

title: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: DPF differential pressure sensor signal dropping in and out.
fullDescription:
P2460 is part of the DPF differential pressure monitor family. The DP sensor measures the pressure drop across the particulate filter and feeds the soot loading model. Faulty readings cause regens to be skipped, repeated, or incorrectly aborted.

Most frequent root cause is plugged or damaged hoses to the sensor — soot and water freeze into the small lines.
safetyImpact: Regen disabled or runs at wrong time; long-term DPF damage possible.

fixSteps.title: Inspect DP sensor hoses
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and blow through; replace if cracked or sooted shut.

fixSteps.title: Compare scan-tool DP reading
fixSteps.instruction: At idle should be near 0 kPa; under load up to 3-15 kPa depending on load.

fixSteps.title: Replace DP sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM part; resets often required.

faq.q: Are the hoses really that fragile?
faq.a: Yes — they get brittle from heat and clog with soot/condensate; they are the #1 cause of DPF DP codes.

title: Crankcase Pressure Too High
shortDescription: Engine crankcase pressure exceeds limits indicating PCV/blowby fault.
fullDescription:
P226A relates to the crankcase pressure circuit on modern diesel and turbo gasoline engines. The crankcase pressure sensor is part of the active CCV (crankcase ventilation) system and helps the ECM diagnose PCV failures and excessive blowby that compromises emissions.

A persistent fault here can mask real engine wear or, conversely, falsely flag a healthy engine.
safetyImpact: Possible oil leaks pushed past seals; long-term engine damage from elevated blowby.

fixSteps.title: Verify sensor reading
fixSteps.instruction: Pressure should be slightly negative or near 0 at idle.

fixSteps.title: Check PCV system
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect hoses and CCV separator for blockage or collapse.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor or PCV unit
fixSteps.instruction: Address the root mechanical cause first.

faq.q: Is high crankcase pressure serious?
faq.a: Yes — sustained elevated pressure pushes oil past seals and can be a sign of worn rings.

title: NOx Exceedence — Reagent Consumption Too Low
shortDescription: Reagent (DEF) consumption rate is below model expectations indicating dosing or storage fault.
fullDescription:
P2BAB is part of the heavy-duty / EU emissions enforcement suite that triggers torque/speed limits when NOx control fails. These codes implement the regulatory inducement strategy: warnings, then 25% torque cut, then 5 mph crawl, then no-restart.

Diagnosis must address the underlying SCR fault — clearing the code without fixing the dosing or sensor issue does nothing because the inducement re-arms within minutes.
safetyImpact: Vehicle inducement active — torque cut or low-speed limp; eventual no-start.

fixSteps.title: Pull full freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: Identify dosing rate, NOx delta, SCR temperature at fault.

fixSteps.title: Run dosing test
fixSteps.instruction: Bidirectional command of dosing pump and verify spray.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed component and reset inducement
fixSteps.instruction: Per OEM repair-verification procedure.

faq.q: Why does my truck slow to 5 mph?
faq.a: Federal and EU regs mandate inducement when NOx control fails — this is a regulated derate, not a fault response.

title: Reductant Pump Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: DEF pump pressure does not match commanded value.
fullDescription:
P3056 relates to the DEF storage and delivery hardware. In sub-freezing climates the tank and lines must be heated above 12°C for dosing to start. A heater fault doesn't immediately stop dosing in warm weather but causes morning cold-start failures and eventually inducement.

Most heater faults are open elements after long service or salt-corroded harness connections at the tank module.
safetyImpact: Possible no-dose at cold start leading to inducement after extended cold operation.

fixSteps.title: Verify heater current draw
fixSteps.instruction: Compare against spec (typically 5-10 A).

fixSteps.title: Inspect tank module connector
fixSteps.instruction: Salt corrosion is endemic on these connectors.

fixSteps.title: Replace heater or tank header
fixSteps.instruction: Often sold only as a header assembly.

faq.q: Why does this only act up in winter?
faq.a: The heaters only run when DEF is below ~12°C; the fault is invisible in warm weather.
